summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for acute worsening of chronic heart failure, presenting with shortness of breath and bilateral leg edema. He reported a 2-pound weight gain and possible increased salt intake. Initial evaluation showed an INR of 3.9, clear lungs on exam, and no signs of infection or pulmonary embolism. An echocardiogram revealed a reduced ejection fraction of 45% with new wall motion abnormalities compared to prior studies, indicating worsening systolic function. He was treated with IV lasix, transitioned to oral diuretics, and discharged on increased furosemide 40 mg twice daily. Warfarin was adjusted to 2.5 mg daily to maintain therapeutic INR. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged home with follow-up arranged for cardiology and primary care.
problems: Acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure
Heart valve replaced by other means
